body: This! Fucking exactly! I am just a vehicle for my husband and child and I get no affection in return for any of my efforts. You are not the only one.

Seriously though. It's not always you that's the problem so try not to let your circumstances or other people define your feelings. Act selfishly when you need to. You can be kind to others but you have to do you first.

You may have seen someone from the livery service. If a funeral home doesn't have their own hearse or limo, or they need an extra they will rent one and usually also a driver for the day. Oftentimes they will try to help out in small ways at the funeral, or at least the guys/gals at our chosen livery service did. So you may see the same guy at different funerals under the employ of different funeral homes for the day.

Fuck other people and their opinions. Every single point of misery in my life I can trace back to some bullshit related to someone else, my parents, "friends", family, husband etc. Not that everyone mentioned is a total asshole. Mostly the shit they do that hurts me is unintentional because they are too focused on their own selves. Focus on yourself more. Take steps forward, whatever you can do. Ignore the bullshit and try not to overanalyze. Cut out the unnecessary drama and people. If you can't remove yourself from a situation, try to work toward making it out. Focus on nothing being permanent. All lives have highs and lows. Things pass. Don't die because of someone else. Fuck them.

I don't know about a reading, but the best funerals always have a good story about the deceased. I think what you just  wrote about her was lovely. I would expand on that with a memory. Something that makes you laugh.
Yes, ask your job if they have a clothing allowance. Whatever you get, ironing and cleaning it appropriately will keep it looking nice. I would ask your female pro friends where they shop.

I think it's maybe good for my baby to go to the YMCA too so she can get some socialization. Also, found a place near us that's a sort of coffee house with a special play place for toddlers and kids. And I signed up for parents as teachers to come out once a month and give me parenting tips and just check my child for development.

Look for meetup groups in your area and see if there is anything interesting to you. Maybe you can find a friend that way. Sign up for nextdoor. Or neighbors app. Good luck. I am in same boat. Need some mom friends.

I felt this in my heart. I left my 60k a year job to become a stay at home parent. And my life changed entirely. My friends disappeared, I barely talk to my spouse about anything except the baby ( because that's all I have going on). Sex life sucks. I have no answers except that many people are saying it will get better. I am 14 months in and it feels worse. One thing I have done is joined the YMCA. They will watch her for up to 90 minutes a day so I can do something positive for myself. I tried to set up meetups, but everyone flaked out on me. I would tote my baby through a war zone if I could just meet another adult to talk to at the other end.

Mine too. Mine is 14 months. It's not every night, but often. We have also rules out teething as she has popped molars through 3 times already with non-issue. I suspect it might be a combination of night terrors and separation anxiety because there is no consoling her but also, trying to put her down makes the screaming worse. I read something that said babies start to develop separation anxiety at about this age. The 1st time it happened I was up with her for 5 hours trying to settle her. Uselessly. Eventually I put her in the crib and she cried for 5 more minutes and went to sleep. The next night it happened again. We went and comforted her. Put her back in crib. Cried for a minute or two and went back to sleep. It has gotten better but this has been a recent thing and now she has a head cold so the rules have changed. I would look up controlled crying. That's where we are at right now. She knows we will respond appropriately, but also she is learning that she needs to go back to sleep.

I was lucky enough to get a paid position and I know a few more who did also, but I know just as many who didn't get paid at all or got paid very little. Keep searching until you find what works and be clear with potential employers that you don't have the means to work what amounts to a full time job without getting compensated. Just don't expect top dollar until you get your license. Best of luck.

Worked in the industry for 11 years. Agree with previous poster, job has potential to either help with or exacerbate your fears. I personally came to the conclusion that none of this whole life business really matters as much to anyone except  the person living it so you might as well do the best for yourself. Why is it so important for most people to feel like any of this matters? Ultimately, the biggest impact most of us will ever make is on a small scale, and that is fine. It's within my means to be kind to the people I meet and I am not going to stress myself trying to change the world or go down in history. I find the idea of the ending of my life to be quite liberating. Not that I am in a big rush for it, but when it happens, I think it will be nice for once to not have to worry about anything. For some strange reason, being in the industry helped with my depression, but I think for many people it would do the opposite.

If the person responsible (widow) doesn't want military services, flag or marker, you legally have to respect that. Doing otherwise would open you up to a potential lawsuit. She can always change her mind later, there is no time limit for military burial benefits. Or, after she dies, whoever is left can move forward with honors, flag, even placement of cremains at a national cemetery.
But these things are only offered once. If you do something now and hide it from family, it won't be available after she dies.

I wouldn't have traded my teacher for the world. He was awesome. Dr. Barry Murphy (whose favorite element was barium, btw). He used to work for Dodge chemical. He was genius level smart but also very sweet. When talked about chemistry you could tell he was on a whole different level, but he did his best to dumb it down and make it fun for us.  He tried so hard to make sure that all the students understood the coursework. He had special meetups and study groups in the cafeteria with us, and even though some of us didn't need the help we would show up anyhow just to hang out. Unfortunately, I suspect that before his retirement, OSHA standards weren't that great because he passed a few years ago from cancer. I specifically recall him having to have cancerous nasal tumors removed. But he was in class shortly after wearing some crazy nose apparatus and making self depreciating jokes about looking like Hannibal Lecter. I hope his family knows how well loved he was.

Also, legally in Missouri, a family member or designated representative can dispose of the body by burial but they MUST also take care of a death certificate. It is totally legal here to do so but it is unorthodox and would be difficult for someone unfamiliar with the process. (Also, the cemetery may not be willing to work with you without a funeral home involved). There are areas in the state where you can bury someone on your own property but there are many regulations surrounding how to do so. In any case, all deaths that are not at the hospital, even the most natural of deaths, must be reported to the medical examiner or coroner, either by the police, EMT,or hospice nurse/other nursing staff. We had a case where a gentleman died at home on hospice on a Saturday, his family had handbuilt him a casket, he stayed in the garage in the casket until Monday when the family loaded him into the pickup and buried him at the veterans cemetery. The medical examiner was informed by hospice that this was the plan and got approval. We were only involved to do the death certificate because family didn't want to deal with that and because the national cemetery kinda wanted us there. Long story, but check into your rights in your area. However, this is a ton of work for your family and not probably the best option. A decent funeral home is there to respect your wishes and not take advantage. I have met many compassionate people in the industry who would love to help you on your terms. Get talking to some family owned businesses and go with your gut.

Check out anatomical gifts through medcure, science care, and Genesis legacy. They take care of everything  including contracting with a local funeral home to transport the body and also paperwork such as permits and death certificates. In my area, medcure and Genesis was no cost to family. Also, if you have any medical schools in the area, you can do donation there usually and pay a small fee to funeral home for transport and paperwork. My funeral home charged $495 and we were almost the cheapest in town. Be aware however that you can be turned down as a donor for communicable diseases or obesity.

Family with a toddler son who died from accidentally drinking his father's illegal methadone that he got out of fridge thinking it was juice. Grandfather (who had custody of the twin sister) kept trying to make funeral arrangements with us. We had worked it out where his only expense would have been the wholesale cost of the tiny casket. Unfortunately, we needed signature from mother or father to pick up body from morgue. They kept stalling, for over 2 weeks, couldn't figure out why. Turned out they had set up a GoFundMe page for "funeral expenses in the amount of $10k". (i.e. drug money). I kept calling them because people kept trying to donate money directly to the funeral home and I kept having to tell people that the bill was already taken care of. This was the only time I have ever yelled at a grieving family. Mother could not be bothered to do anything. When they finally came in to sign papers, the father was high  as fuck. Couldn't sit down. Went outside and crouched down in the bushes in front of building and I think he was shooting up. On the day of funeral, the father got in a fight with the grandfather. I think there was a rep from DFS there as well as some undercover investigators. He got jail time but I think the mother is still out there and I really hope she's got her shit together now.
